ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, quadrilateral ABCD is a square, with diagonals AC and BD intersecting at point O. Point E is any point on AD other than the endpoints. A line is drawn from point O such that $OF \perp OE$ and intersects CD at point F. If $AB=6$, what is the area of quadrilateral EOFD?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since quadrilateral ABCD is a square, \\
it follows that OA=OB=OC=OD, AC$\perp$BD, $\angle$ODA=$\angle$OCD=45$^\circ$,\\
Since OE$\perp$OF,\\
it follows that $\angle$EOF=$\angle$COD=90$^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle$EOD=$\angle$FOC,\\
thus $\triangle$EOD$\cong$$\triangle$FOC,\\
therefore the area of $\triangle$EOD = the area of $\triangle$FOC,\\
Since OA=OB and $\angle$AOB=90$^\circ$,\\
it follows that 2OA$^{2}$=AB$^{2}$=6$^{2}$,\\
Solving for OA$^{2}$ gives 18,\\
Since the area of quadrilateral EOFD = area of $\triangle$EOD + area of $\triangle$FOD = area of $\triangle$FOC + area of $\triangle$FOD = area of $\triangle$COD,\\
Therefore, the area of quadrilateral EOFD = $\frac{1}{2}OD^{2}=\frac{1}{2}OA^{2}=\boxed{9}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a square ABCD, A is at the upper left, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, D is at the upper right; the two diagonals AC and BD intersect at the center O. Point E is located on the upper side AD, point F is located on the right side CD, and the line segments OE and OF are drawn, where the problem statement gives OE ⟂ OF. The region sought is the quadrilateral EOFD enclosed by E, O, F, D. Reasoning: The diagonals of a square are perpendicular to each other and bisect each other, so OD=OC, and ∠DOC=90°. Also because OE ⟂ OF, ∠EOF=90°. Comparing these two right angles around point O, we can get ∠EOD=∠FOC. The diagonals of a square make a 45° angle with the sides, therefore ∠EDO=45°, ∠FCO=45°, so ∠EDO=∠FCO. Thus triangle EOD and triangle FOC have OD=OC, and the corresponding angles at the two ends are equal, hence △EOD≅△FOC, so their areas are equal. Therefore, area(EOFD)=area(△EOD)+area(△FOD)=area(△FOC)+area(△FOD)=area(△COD). And △COD is one of the four congruent triangles into which the two diagonals of the square divide it, so its area is equal to one fourth of the area of the square. AB=6, the area of the square is 6^2=36, therefore area(△COD)=36/4=9.
